title: Thrive Capital’s first investor letter shows how completely OpenAI has come to define it
excerpt: A Thrive Capital fund has swelled to about $3.7bn on OpenAI and SpaceX bets, Joshua Kushner’s first formal investor letter reveals, and the firm is quietly selling part of its OpenAI stake.
content_html:
Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital has sent its first formal letter to investors, and the standout figure captures the AI era in miniature.

One of its funds has swelled to about $3.7bn in value, driven overwhelmingly by early bets on OpenAI and SpaceX. The letter, reported by Bloomberg, reads as a victory lap and a quiet hedge at the same time.

That Thrive is writing to its backers at all is notable in itself. Kushner has built one of the most secretive and sought-after firms in venture capital, so a formal letter, complete with hard marks and a candid line on concentration, is a departure that doubles as a statement of confidence.

It also lands at a moment when the whole industry is arguing about whether AI valuations reflect real value or collective hope, which makes a firm this exposed to a single name showing its workings all the more striking.

Thrive’s OpenAI position is practically a chronicle of the boom. The firm first backed the company in 2022 at a $29bn valuation, led a tender the following year at $86bn, and has since committed around a billion dollars more across rounds that valued OpenAI at $150bn and then $285bn.

With the company now lining up a trillion-dollar listing, those early entries have multiplied many times over, at least on paper.

That $3.7bn mark also owes a great deal to Thrive’s stake in Elon Musk’s SpaceX, another private giant whose valuation has climbed relentlessly.

Between them, two holdings now account for the bulk of the fund’s gains, a concentration most portfolio managers would flinch at and Thrive is presenting as vindication.

There is a large asterisk, though. Almost none of that value has actually been banked. The gains are unrealised marks, dependent on OpenAI’s and SpaceX’s private valuations continuing to rise, and a growing share of Thrive’s paper returns now rests on OpenAI alone.

On paper, the firm is having a spectacular decade, but in cash, far less has been settled, and paper fortunes have a habit of shrinking the moment the market that created them turns.

Which is what makes the other disclosure in the letter so telling. Thrive is selling part of its OpenAI stake, taking some chips off the table even as it insists the story is only beginning.

Trimming a winner is textbook risk management, yet it also quietly concedes the oldest truth in venture capital, which is that a mark is not money until someone else pays for it.

Thrive has grown into a heavyweight on the strength of these wagers. The firm now manages roughly $25bn and this year closed a record $10bn fund, its largest yet and reportedly oversubscribed, a sign that limited partners are content to keep feeding a strategy built on a handful of enormous private positions.

Kushner has also spun up a separate vehicle, Thrive Holdings, to buy up traditional services firms and rewire them with AI.

The letter arrives at a jittery moment for that whole model. As doubts grow about whether AI revenues can ever justify the valuations, and about whether much of the sector is a bubble waiting to deflate, funds whose fortunes hinge on a single soaring private mark start to look exposed rather than clever.

Thrive’s numbers dazzle precisely because OpenAI’s have never stopped climbing.

For now, it stands as one of the great venture bets of the age. Kushner backed OpenAI when it was still a curiosity and rode it to the centre of the economy.

What the letter cannot answer is what happens to a fund like this on the day OpenAI’s private valuation finally stops rising, because a return that exists only as a mark can evaporate almost as fast as it appeared.

content_html_zh:
约书亚·库什纳 (Joshua Kushner) 的 Thrive Capital 向投资者发出了第一封正式信函，这位杰出人物捕捉到了人工智能时代的缩影。

在 OpenAI 和 SpaceX 的早期押注的推动下，其一只基金的价值已膨胀至约 37 亿美元。 据彭博社报道，这封信读起来既是胜利的一圈，又是安静的对冲。

Thrive 写信给其支持者本身就值得注意。 库什纳建立了风险投资领域最隐秘、最受追捧的公司之一，因此一封正式的信函，带有明确的标记和关于集中度的坦诚路线，既是一种背离，也是一种信心声明。

与此同时，整个行业都在争论人工智能的估值是否反映了真正的价值或集体的希望，这使得一家以单一名字展示其运作方式的公司显得更加引人注目。

Thrive 的 OpenAI 地位实际上是繁荣的编年史。 该公司于 2022 年首次以 290 亿美元的估值支持该公司，并于次年以 860 亿美元的估值牵头进行了招标，此后又在各轮融资中追加了约 10 亿美元的投资，对 OpenAI 的估值分别为 1500 亿美元和 2850 亿美元。

随着该公司现在准备进行数万亿美元的上市，这些早期进入的股票已经成倍增加，至少在纸面上是这样。

这 37 亿美元的大关在很大程度上也要归功于 Thrive 持有埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 旗下 SpaceX 的股份，这是另一家估值不断攀升的私人巨头。

目前，这两只股票占据了该基金收益的大部分，大多数投资组合经理都会对这一集中感到畏惧，而 Thrive 则证明了这一点。

不过，有一个大星号。 这些价值实际上几乎没有被存入银行。 这些收益是未实现的，依赖于 OpenAI 和 SpaceX 的私人估值持续上升，而 Thrive 的纸面回报中越来越多的份额现在仅依赖于 OpenAI。

从账面上看，该公司正在经历辉煌的十年，但从现金角度来看，结算的情况要少得多，而账面财富往往会在创造它们的市场转向时缩水。

这就是信中的其他披露如此有说服力的原因。 尽管 Thrive 坚称故事才刚刚开始，但它正在出售部分 OpenAI 股份，从而拿走了一些筹码。

削减赢家是教科书式的风险管理，但它也悄悄承认了风险投资中最古老的真理，即除非有人付钱，否则分数就不是金钱。

凭借这些赌注，Thrive 已成长为重量级企业。 该公司目前管理着大约 250 亿美元，今年关闭了创纪录的 100 亿美元基金，这是迄今为止规模最大的基金，据报道已经超额认购，这表明有限合伙人愿意继续支持建立在少数巨额私人头寸基础上的战略。

库什纳还成立了一家独立的公司 Thrive Holdings，收购传统服务公司并用人工智能对它们进行重组。

这封信是在整个模型感到紧张的时刻送达的。 随着人们越来越怀疑人工智能收入是否能够证明其估值合理，以及该行业的大部分是否是一个等待破灭的泡沫，那些命运取决于单一飙升的私人马克的基金开始显得暴露而不是聪明。

Thrive 的数字令人眼花缭乱，正是因为 OpenAI 的数字从未停止攀升。

目前，它是这个时代最大的风险投资之一。 当 OpenAI 还只是一种好奇时，库什纳就支持了它，并将其推向了经济的中心。

这封信无法回答的是，当 OpenAI 的私人估值最终停止上涨之日，这样的基金会发生什么，因为仅作为标记存在的回报几乎会像它出现时一样快地消失。
